initial_state.accepted_at_basis: IMMUTABLE_SNAPSHOT_COMMIT_DATE_PROXY; the original proposal acceptance date is not established

assumptions.text: Motivating premise stated in the 2023 KEP text: because PodSpec container resources are immutable, changing a Pod's resource allocation requires recreating the Pod.

constraints_dependencies.text: Explicit non-goal: controlling the full lifecycle of a Pod whose in-place resize failed; this is left to the actors that initiated the resize.
Changing a Pod's QoS class without a restart is a non-goal.
Changing Init Container resources without a restart is a non-goal.
Evicting lower-priority Pods to make room for a resize is a non-goal (noted as a possible future enhancement).
In-place resize is restricted to CPU and memory; updating extended resources or any other resource type is a non-goal.
Supporting CPU/memory manager policies other than the default 'None' policy is a non-goal.

initial_state.decision: Support changing CPU and memory resources for running Pods without mandatory Pod or container recreation.

goals.text: Permit CPU and memory resource requests/limits to change in place, without requiring a Pod or container restart.
Allow actors (e.g., users, VPA, StatefulSet, JobController) to decide how to proceed when an in-place resource resize is not possible.
Change the UpdateContainerResources CRI API to take a platform-agnostic ContainerResources parameter so that it works for Windows containers and other non-Linux runtimes, not only Linux.
Extend the ContainerStatus CRI API so the kubelet can query the CPU and memory configuration currently applied to a container.
Define, as a high-level guide rather than a detailed implementation specification, the expected behavior of a container runtime when handling resource updates.

implementation_scope.text: Represent desired resources through mutable PodSpec fields and report allocated/applied resources through PodStatus.
Offer per-resource restart-policy choices to control how container resizes are attempted.
Model resize operation progress through states such as proposed, in progress, deferred and infeasible.

original_alternatives_not_encoded_as_out.description: Scheduler approval of resize was considered; rationale for rejecting it is not documented in this short section.
Checkpointing allocated resources in PodSpec was considered; rationale for rejecting it is not documented in this short section.

quality_attributes.text: Avoid service disruption for stateful, batch, and low-replica workloads; availability and cost are stated concerns.

initial_state.rationale_time_note: The pinned 2023 snapshot predates the selected 2024 commit window; the original KEP approval is not proven by the snapshot time.

requirements.text: Distinguish the desired resources declared in the Pod spec from the resources allocated to the Pod on the node and from the actual resources applied to its containers.

Expose, for each resized container resource, why the desired and actual resources differ: whether a proposed resize has not yet been accepted or rejected by the kubelet, has been accepted and is being actuated, is deferred, or has been rejected as infeasible; supplemented by Pod Events at key steps.

initial_state.review_instructions: Verify all paraphrased statements against the pinned snapshot, confirm chronology and actual acceptance separately, remove conjecture, and only then explicitly approve a revision for controlled experiments.

runtime_cutoff_audit.description: Cutoff changed ONLY for retrospective auditable evidence retrieval

artifact_review_records.reason: The added table-of-contents entry supplies navigation, not a changed architectural claim or new support for any fixed-S0 element.
The added alternatives-section navigation entry does not itself adopt, justify, replace, or retire a fixed-S0 claim.

The core design summary removes allocated resources from the resources reported through PodStatus. The same-event API section establishes the ordinary replacement and preserves the separately gated alpha field.

The API design explicitly replaces ordinary allocated-resource status reporting with local caching/checkpointing and separately gates the residual alpha status field. Actual-resource reporting and the logical resource distinctions survive.

The backward-compatibility explanation changes its public source of truth from allocated resources in AllocatedResources to actual configurations in Resources. This locally reflects the narrowed ordinary PodStatus reporting contract.
The admission description removes the ordinary write of admitted requests to container status while retaining the internal allocation checkpoint.

The local change replaces the input used for kubelet re-admission with allocations restored from a checkpoint. I1 specifies reporting through PodStatus, not the source used for re-admission. The protection of previously admitted Pods survives unchanged, so this is neither fresh support for Q1 nor evidence that its qualified availability goal has weakened.

The hunk changes scheduler accounting inputs and how InProgress is treated. It does not itself change which quantities are reported, retire the desired/allocated/actual distinction, or newly introduce the progress-state model. These consumer-side changes do not establish a material effect on an exact fixed-S0 clause.

The accounting rule switches consumers from AllocatedResources to Resources while retaining the same anti-race rationale. Fixed S0 does not prescribe that accounting input. Existing Resources reporting is not newly operationalised, and the unchanged CPU-manager caveat supplies no fresh effect.

The deleted note concerns the requests-only field and internal checkpointing of limits. The captured event continues to specify checkpointing admitted requests and limits. Removing this relocated explanation does not independently retire a fixed-S0 requirement or establish a new supporting premise.

The changes revise quota accounting, status-update triggers, and a component checklist. Fixed S0 does not choose these accounting formulas or require initialization of AllocatedResources on Create. The hunk does not independently establish a replacement of the reporting contract; the surviving validation and resize-policy entries are invariants, not fresh evidence.

The scheduler checklist changes its accounting input to actual Status.Resources. That is a consumer implementation change, not a local change to I1's reporting mechanism or R1's required distinctions. The unchanged Linux/Windows CRI statement is not new support for G3a.

The completed-state expression replaces a status-field reference with the conceptual allocated quantity. Successful completion still equates desired, allocated, and actual resources. This preserves the completion invariant rather than introducing a new state model or independently changing public reporting.

The addition discusses conditional alternatives for an allocated-status API. No alternative is adopted here. Its benefits and costs concern particular candidate fields, type choices, migration paths, and container-versus-Pod granularity; they do not establish retirement or incompatibility with a fixed-S0 requirement. Nor do they directly reduce the justification of S0's broad PodStatus reporting choice: several costs arise specifically from proposed representations that S0 does not choose. Prospective DRA support does not supersede the CPU/memory-only scope.

The added instrumentation counts Pod-level resize requests and transitions of an existing resize-status model. It provides aggregate monitoring, not a newly adopted model of resize progress (I3), per-container explanations and Events (R2), or a new distinction between desired, allocated, and applied resources (R1). The completion equality references those existing resource representations without changing or independently validating them. No material change to the other fixed elements is established.

The changed lines replace commas with periods in existing beta graduation criteria. VPA integration and tests covering resize policy remain the same criteria; the hunk supplies neither completed validation nor a new mechanism for actor choice or restart-policy control. The unchanged CRI and subresource statements cannot establish a target-local effect. No fixed element is materially affected.

The sole change corrects 'atleast' to 'at least' in an existing user-feedback graduation criterion. It does not introduce actual feedback, validation results, a rationale, or an architectural change concerning any fixed element.

The hunk clarifies default-behavior documentation by naming status fields the kubelet sets, formats the feature-gate name, removes an unused enablement template, and advises against disabling the feature on a running node. The status-field statement describes the existing reporting representation rather than establishing a newly introduced mechanism or validation of I1 or R1; applied-resource reporting already appears in unchanged text. The node-level feature-disable caveat does not change the restart requirements for resizing a running Pod, and Q1 does not guarantee disruption-free feature rollback. No material effect on another fixed element is established.

The additions fill operational-readiness sections with rollback indicators, a planned upgrade/rollback test sequence, monitoring guidance, SLO suggestions, and a compatible-runtime dependency. Expected test outcomes are not observed validation of restart-free resizing or workload availability. Aggregate resize metrics monitor existing states rather than newly modelling progress or supplying the per-container explanations and Events required by R2. The runtime dependency does not establish any specific platform-agnostic CRI change, status-query extension, or runtime-update behavior guide. These operational additions do not materially change or newly substantiate the exact fixed targets.

The added outage guidance distinguishes requests not submitted, requests awaiting kubelet observation, and potentially stale PodStatus after observation while the kubelet retains internal resource state. R1 and I1 require resource distinctions and status reporting, not continuously current reporting during API outages; R2 likewise does not assert an all-condition availability guarantee. Thus the caveat does not establish incompatibility or reduced justification for those exact obligations. Log-troubleshooting guidance and replacement of the failure-mode template with TBD do not change the remaining fixed elements.
The target-local change only renumbers two validation rules. Their obligations remain identical before and after; it supplies no new mechanism, justification, or evidence for any fixed-S0 element.

The change replaces mutable ResizePolicy entries with append-only entries, permitting additions for newly present resources. I2 requires per-resource restart-policy choices, but does not require subsequent modification of existing choices or an entry for every resource. The changed mutability rule therefore does not replace or retire a fixed-S0 claim. The passage also does not change the mutability of desired resource fields asserted by I1.

The sidecar edit corrects terminology; permission to resize restartable InitContainers and the exclusion of non-restartable InitContainers already appear before the change. It therefore does not newly contradict C2b. QoS-class immutability likewise survives unchanged: emphasis and the distinction between QoS Class and QoS Shape do not alter C2a. Explicitly requiring both CPU and memory for Guaranteed shape clarifies validation, rather than newly establishing the fixed prohibition on changing actual QoS class without restart. No other fixed-S0 claim has a demonstrated material delta.

The hunk replaces checkpointing the original QoS class with status persistence and permitted recovery from status after kubelet restart. Fixed S0 does not choose checkpointing as its QoS-preservation mechanism, so this is an implementation change rather than replacement of C2a. I1 concerns allocated/applied resources in PodStatus, not storage of QoS identity. The future-enhancement reference does not adopt a change to either target.

The additions are future-enhancement design sketches, not adopted controller-resize or explicit-QoS mechanisms. The controller policy discussion does not newly operationalise G2 or I2, and it provides no explicit rationale for their exact qualified obligations. The mixed-QoS replica example documents a prospective workload-resize complication, but its suggested mitigation preserves recreation when changing QoS class; it neither supersedes C2a nor establishes a reduction in the feasibility of the qualified fixed-S0 in-place-resize goal. Removing a future-work item about updating limits does not retire G1's existing CPU/memory request-and-limit goal. No material effect on the remaining fixed elements is established.

A0001:P0001 changes ResizePolicy from append-only (A0001:L0005–L0006) to mutable, while retaining append as the strictly necessary capability and qualifying full mutability as subject to reevaluation (A0001:L0007–L0009). I2 requires per-resource restart-policy choices but does not prescribe whether those choices are append-only or mutable; this change therefore does not replace or materially alter the fixed target claim. I1 concerns mutable desired resource values and allocated/applied resource reporting, not mutation of ResizePolicy. The retained restart behavior is unchanged context, not fresh evidence. No material effect on any other fixed-S0 element is established by this local change.

The local change moves latest-milestone and the beta milestone from v1.33 to v1.32. This is release bookkeeping, not a change to any fixed-S0 architectural obligation, mechanism, or supporting rationale. The unchanged beta stage supplies no fresh evidence of target fulfillment.

The local change registers InPlacePodVerticalScalingAllocatedStatus for kube-apiserver and kubelet. Although its name relates to allocated-resource status, the passage does not specify gate behavior, defaults, reporting semantics, or replacement of an existing representation. Registration alone therefore establishes neither a new operationalisation of R1 or I1 nor retirement or replacement of their material claims. No material effect on the other fixed-S0 elements is established.

Reviewed against every fixed-S0 element. The only local change adds an author. Authorship bookkeeping neither changes an architectural claim nor introduces evidence, rationale, or an adopted mechanism supporting any fixed-S0 obligation.

Reviewed against every fixed-S0 element. The local changes update stage from alpha to beta, latest milestone from v1.30 to v1.31, and the stable milestone from v1.32 to TBD. These lifecycle metadata changes do not establish validation of any exact S0 claim or change its mechanism, scope, or justification. The unchanged feature-gate name supplies no fresh evidence. The unspecified stable milestone does not itself weaken the feasibility of the fixed architectural obligations, which contain no release deadline.

independent_artifact_reviews.reason: The added table-of-contents entry supplies navigation, not a changed architectural claim or new support for any fixed-S0 element.
The added alternatives-section navigation entry does not itself adopt, justify, replace, or retire a fixed-S0 claim.

The core design summary removes allocated resources from the resources reported through PodStatus. The same-event API section establishes the ordinary replacement and preserves the separately gated alpha field.

The API design explicitly replaces ordinary allocated-resource status reporting with local caching/checkpointing and separately gates the residual alpha status field. Actual-resource reporting and the logical resource distinctions survive.

The backward-compatibility explanation changes its public source of truth from allocated resources in AllocatedResources to actual configurations in Resources. This locally reflects the narrowed ordinary PodStatus reporting contract.
The admission description removes the ordinary write of admitted requests to container status while retaining the internal allocation checkpoint.

The local change replaces the input used for kubelet re-admission with allocations restored from a checkpoint. I1 specifies reporting through PodStatus, not the source used for re-admission. The protection of previously admitted Pods survives unchanged, so this is neither fresh support for Q1 nor evidence that its qualified availability goal has weakened.

The hunk changes scheduler accounting inputs and how InProgress is treated. It does not itself change which quantities are reported, retire the desired/allocated/actual distinction, or newly introduce the progress-state model. These consumer-side changes do not establish a material effect on an exact fixed-S0 clause.

The accounting rule switches consumers from AllocatedResources to Resources while retaining the same anti-race rationale. Fixed S0 does not prescribe that accounting input. Existing Resources reporting is not newly operationalised, and the unchanged CPU-manager caveat supplies no fresh effect.

The deleted note concerns the requests-only field and internal checkpointing of limits. The captured event continues to specify checkpointing admitted requests and limits. Removing this relocated explanation does not independently retire a fixed-S0 requirement or establish a new supporting premise.

The changes revise quota accounting, status-update triggers, and a component checklist. Fixed S0 does not choose these accounting formulas or require initialization of AllocatedResources on Create. The hunk does not independently establish a replacement of the reporting contract; the surviving validation and resize-policy entries are invariants, not fresh evidence.

The scheduler checklist changes its accounting input to actual Status.Resources. That is a consumer implementation change, not a local change to I1's reporting mechanism or R1's required distinctions. The unchanged Linux/Windows CRI statement is not new support for G3a.

The completed-state expression replaces a status-field reference with the conceptual allocated quantity. Successful completion still equates desired, allocated, and actual resources. This preserves the completion invariant rather than introducing a new state model or independently changing public reporting.

The addition discusses conditional alternatives for an allocated-status API. No alternative is adopted here. Its benefits and costs concern particular candidate fields, type choices, migration paths, and container-versus-Pod granularity; they do not establish retirement or incompatibility with a fixed-S0 requirement. Nor do they directly reduce the justification of S0's broad PodStatus reporting choice: several costs arise specifically from proposed representations that S0 does not choose. Prospective DRA support does not supersede the CPU/memory-only scope.

The added instrumentation counts Pod-level resize requests and transitions of an existing resize-status model. It provides aggregate monitoring, not a newly adopted model of resize progress (I3), per-container explanations and Events (R2), or a new distinction between desired, allocated, and applied resources (R1). The completion equality references those existing resource representations without changing or independently validating them. No material change to the other fixed elements is established.

The changed lines replace commas with periods in existing beta graduation criteria. VPA integration and tests covering resize policy remain the same criteria; the hunk supplies neither completed validation nor a new mechanism for actor choice or restart-policy control. The unchanged CRI and subresource statements cannot establish a target-local effect. No fixed element is materially affected.

The sole change corrects 'atleast' to 'at least' in an existing user-feedback graduation criterion. It does not introduce actual feedback, validation results, a rationale, or an architectural change concerning any fixed element.

The hunk clarifies default-behavior documentation by naming status fields the kubelet sets, formats the feature-gate name, removes an unused enablement template, and advises against disabling the feature on a running node. The status-field statement describes the existing reporting representation rather than establishing a newly introduced mechanism or validation of I1 or R1; applied-resource reporting already appears in unchanged text. The node-level feature-disable caveat does not change the restart requirements for resizing a running Pod, and Q1 does not guarantee disruption-free feature rollback. No material effect on another fixed element is established.

The additions fill operational-readiness sections with rollback indicators, a planned upgrade/rollback test sequence, monitoring guidance, SLO suggestions, and a compatible-runtime dependency. Expected test outcomes are not observed validation of restart-free resizing or workload availability. Aggregate resize metrics monitor existing states rather than newly modelling progress or supplying the per-container explanations and Events required by R2. The runtime dependency does not establish any specific platform-agnostic CRI change, status-query extension, or runtime-update behavior guide. These operational additions do not materially change or newly substantiate the exact fixed targets.

The added outage guidance distinguishes requests not submitted, requests awaiting kubelet observation, and potentially stale PodStatus after observation while the kubelet retains internal resource state. R1 and I1 require resource distinctions and status reporting, not continuously current reporting during API outages; R2 likewise does not assert an all-condition availability guarantee. Thus the caveat does not establish incompatibility or reduced justification for those exact obligations. Log-troubleshooting guidance and replacement of the failure-mode template with TBD do not change the remaining fixed elements.
The target-local change only renumbers two validation rules. Their obligations remain identical before and after; it supplies no new mechanism, justification, or evidence for any fixed-S0 element.

The change replaces mutable ResizePolicy entries with append-only entries, permitting additions for newly present resources. I2 requires per-resource restart-policy choices, but does not require subsequent modification of existing choices or an entry for every resource. The changed mutability rule therefore does not replace or retire a fixed-S0 claim. The passage also does not change the mutability of desired resource fields asserted by I1.

The sidecar edit corrects terminology; permission to resize restartable InitContainers and the exclusion of non-restartable InitContainers already appear before the change. It therefore does not newly contradict C2b. QoS-class immutability likewise survives unchanged: emphasis and the distinction between QoS Class and QoS Shape do not alter C2a. Explicitly requiring both CPU and memory for Guaranteed shape clarifies validation, rather than newly establishing the fixed prohibition on changing actual QoS class without restart. No other fixed-S0 claim has a demonstrated material delta.

The hunk replaces checkpointing the original QoS class with status persistence and permitted recovery from status after kubelet restart. Fixed S0 does not choose checkpointing as its QoS-preservation mechanism, so this is an implementation change rather than replacement of C2a. I1 concerns allocated/applied resources in PodStatus, not storage of QoS identity. The future-enhancement reference does not adopt a change to either target.

The additions are future-enhancement design sketches, not adopted controller-resize or explicit-QoS mechanisms. The controller policy discussion does not newly operationalise G2 or I2, and it provides no explicit rationale for their exact qualified obligations. The mixed-QoS replica example documents a prospective workload-resize complication, but its suggested mitigation preserves recreation when changing QoS class; it neither supersedes C2a nor establishes a reduction in the feasibility of the qualified fixed-S0 in-place-resize goal. Removing a future-work item about updating limits does not retire G1's existing CPU/memory request-and-limit goal. No material effect on the remaining fixed elements is established.

A0001:P0001 changes ResizePolicy from append-only (A0001:L0005–L0006) to mutable, while retaining append as the strictly necessary capability and qualifying full mutability as subject to reevaluation (A0001:L0007–L0009). I2 requires per-resource restart-policy choices but does not prescribe whether those choices are append-only or mutable; this change therefore does not replace or materially alter the fixed target claim. I1 concerns mutable desired resource values and allocated/applied resource reporting, not mutation of ResizePolicy. The retained restart behavior is unchanged context, not fresh evidence. No material effect on any other fixed-S0 element is established by this local change.

The local change moves latest-milestone and the beta milestone from v1.33 to v1.32. This is release bookkeeping, not a change to any fixed-S0 architectural obligation, mechanism, or supporting rationale. The unchanged beta stage supplies no fresh evidence of target fulfillment.

The local change registers InPlacePodVerticalScalingAllocatedStatus for kube-apiserver and kubelet. Although its name relates to allocated-resource status, the passage does not specify gate behavior, defaults, reporting semantics, or replacement of an existing representation. Registration alone therefore establishes neither a new operationalisation of R1 or I1 nor retirement or replacement of their material claims. No material effect on the other fixed-S0 elements is established.

Reviewed against every fixed-S0 element. The only local change adds an author. Authorship bookkeeping neither changes an architectural claim nor introduces evidence, rationale, or an adopted mechanism supporting any fixed-S0 obligation.
